kyoto_kamesuehiro.gf_detail: Ask. Dry sweets (rakugan of rice flour and brown rice), fresh sweets and yokan, and a senbei-manju of mochi wafer; no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
kyoto_kamesuehiro.vegan_detail: Ask. Bean-paste and sugar sweets are likely candidates, but no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
kyoto_kamesuehiro.hours_raw: 9:00–17:00, Mon, Tue and Thu–Sat; closed Wednesday, Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Takeaway only (Tabelog). Fresh sweets keep only to the day, the senbei-manju to the next day (August–September 2026). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog). On Aneyakoji-dori, 3 min from Karasuma-Oike Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_kamesuehiro.notes: [Wagashi · Karasuma-Oike, a confectioner since 1804] Behind an old shopfront near the Shinpukan, a quiet, old-fashioned shop where the staff explain each sweet in a soft Kyoto lilt. It is known for refined dry sweets — the seasonal boxed assortment and delicate rakugan — and for fresh sweets that must be eaten the same day; the senbei-manju (¥300), crisp mochi wafers filled with bean paste as you buy, is the local favourite. Takeaway only; cash only; closed Wednesdays, Sundays and holidays. A September 2026 buyer found the wrapping and handling careless.

kyoto_sushi_matsumoto_gion.notes: [Sushi · Gion, Kyoto's Edomae counter] Through an indigo noren on the Yayoi-koji lane, a white-wood counter of seven where Daiten Matsumoto, from Kanagawa and trained at Tokyo's Shinbashi Shimizu, makes true Edomae sushi: red-vinegar rice with no sugar, kombu-cured sea bream, kohada, simmered Kuwana clams, anago with tsume, served briskly piece by piece. 2026 reviewers call it Michelin-starred and good value, with more locals than tourists. Omakase only; book by phone or Ikyu; no strong perfume. About ¥20,000–30,000.

kyoto_isshisoden_nakamura.gf_detail: Ask when booking: courses only, and the restaurant asks for dislikes in advance (Tabelog). The signature white-miso zoni is made without dashi (official site); other dishes use soy and miso.
kyoto_isshisoden_nakamura.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-centred Kyoto kaiseki, including the signature sake-grilled guji (official site).
kyoto_isshisoden_nakamura.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–14:00; dinner from 17:00, last entry 19:30; closed Sunday except for parties of 10 or more (Tabelog). No dinner closing time is published, so no hours are stored. Reservations accepted, by phone 075-221-5511; courses only, so mention dislikes when booking (Tabelog). 67 seats with private rooms (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (Tabelog). On Tomikoji-dori just south of Oike, 1 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn west exit (official site; April 2025 review).
kyoto_isshisoden_nakamura.notes: [Kaiseki · Oike, two hundred years of Kyoto ryori] Behind a white noren on Tomikoji-dori, a house that began in 1827 when the first master carried Wakasa fish along the 鯖街道 (the mackerel road) to the palace and court nobles. Sixth-generation 中村元計 (Motokazu Nakamura) — once a Zen trainee at 天龍寺 and now a doctor of food science — keeps the two dishes passed from father to son: sake-grilled guji, finished as a soup with hot water over the bones, and a white-miso zoni made without dashi. Courses are served in quiet private rooms over a courtyard; reviewers note three Michelin stars. Lunch around ¥20,000–30,000, dinner ¥40,000–50,000; book ahead; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Motokazu Nakamura (中村元計; official site, sixth-generation master, with the romaji Motokazu Nakamura)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: founded in Bunsei 10 (1827) when the first master, 若狭屋清兵衛, carried Wakasa fish such as guji and mackerel to Kyoto for the palace and court nobles; the second generation began catering; the third, a tea devotee, made tea kaiseki catering the core; the fourth supplied the inns 柊家, 俵屋 and 炭家 during the war; after the war the restaurant opened on its present site, and the fifth generation built today's base. The sixth, 中村元計, studied at Tokyo University of Fisheries, trained as a Zen monk at 天龍寺 in 嵯峨嵐山, and in 2021 earned a doctorate in food and agricultural science at 龍谷大学, approaching cooking as science. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2023; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021. 2026 reviews call it Michelin three-starred.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「即味心也」 — taste is the heart: only a person's heart moves another's (official site).

anecdotes.text: "This restaurant has been awarded three Michelin stars for six consecutive years." — October 2026.

Lunch ¥9,800, ¥14,000, ¥18,000 or ¥22,000; dinner ¥14,000, ¥18,000, ¥22,000 or ¥27,000, tax included, from January 2026 (official site); no service charge (Tabelog). 8 counter seats (official site). kyoto_aoike.notes: [French · Imperial Palace south, the vegetable French counter] An old Kyoto townhouse remade under 中村義明 of the sukiya builder 中村外二工務店, with a patchwork zelkova counter of eight seats, Danish chairs and Venetian glass on the table. The chef grows and picks some sixty kinds of vegetables each morning, and the light, consommé-seasoned courses are built around them — the signature terrine of separately cooked vegetables wrapped in cabbage, vegetable mousses, then fish or Omi beef. You leave light. Lunch from ¥9,800, dinner from ¥14,000, tax included and no service charge. Book by phone or Ikyu; no children 10 and under; closed Sundays.

kyoto_kakou_okamoto.notes: [Kaiseki · Higashiyama, a couple's eight-seat counter] Away from the tourist streets near the Umacho bus stop, a couple run an eight-seat counter with one omakase a night; the owner-chef, Ryota Okamoto, trained at Kyoto's HANA Kiccho and Akiyama. Expect deep dashi, playful touches borrowed from French cooking, signatures like shark-fin noodles in chapon broth and natural karasumi, and a long sake list poured to match. Regulars praise the chef's stories and the couple's hospitality; one has been 35 times. About ¥20,000–30,000; book by phone; closed Mondays.

kyoto_sabo_isehan.gf_detail: Ask. Shaved ice, anmitsu, zenzai and matcha are mostly bean, agar and rice-flour sweets, but the parfait has soba cookies and the monaka is a wafer; no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
kyoto_sabo_isehan.vegan_detail: Ask. Azuki, agar, matcha and shiratama may suit; soft serve, condensed milk and cream do not (2026 reviews).
kyoto_sabo_isehan.hours_raw: 11:00–18:30 (last order 18:00); closed Tuesday unless a holiday (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog); a short wait at busy times (September 2026). 26 seats (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards, UnionPay and many QR payments (Tabelog). Parking validation for nearby car parks with a ¥1,500+ purchase (Tabelog). 5 min from Demachiyanagi Stn; 1 min from the Kawaramachi-Imadegawa bus stop; across the road from Demachi Futaba (Tabelog; September 2026).
kyoto_sabo_isehan.notes: [Sweets · Demachi, azuki and matcha across from Futaba] While the queue snakes outside Demachi Futaba, many locals cross the road to this calm sweets café for bowls of azuki and matcha: generous Tanba dainagon beans cooked soft but whole, Uji matcha syrup over shaved ice, chilled zenzai with matcha jelly, anmitsu with soft serve. Matcha is whisked to order and served with a monaka. A good stop after Shimogamo Shrine or Kibune. Around ¥1,000–1,600; cards and QR payments accepted; closed Tuesdays.

roles: Sweets café; no person is named in the sources

anecdotes.text: "The beans are cooked to perfection, maintaining their shape while being soft, and the gentle sweetness is exquisite." — September 2026.
"There were hardly any inbound tourists; it was mostly locals. Meanwhile, the nearby Demachi Futaba had a long line." — October 2026.
"The matcha is prepared one cup at a time upon ordering" — September 2026.

kyoto_honke_gepaikeya_naomasa.gf_detail: Ask. The warabi mochi is described as made with real bracken starch, filled with bean paste and coated in kinako; other sweets vary; no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
kyoto_honke_gepaikeya_naomasa.vegan_detail: Ask. Bean-paste and starch sweets are likely candidates, but no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
kyoto_honke_gepaikeya_naomasa.hours_raw: 10:30–18:00, Mon, Tue and Fri–Sun; closed Wednesday and Thursday (Tabelog). Takeaway only (Tabelog). The warabi mochi is usually ready from 12:30 and sells out to reservations — phone ahead (075-231-0175) or reserve in person the day before; same-day reservations are sometimes possible (September 2026 reviews). Eat it the same day (September 2026). Cash only (Tabelog). On Kiyamachi-dori just north of Sanjo, 155 m from Sanjo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_honke_gepaikeya_naomasa.notes: [Wagashi · Kiyamachi-Sanjo, the warabi mochi worth reserving] A small, old-fashioned sweets shop on Kiyamachi whose warabi mochi is the draw: melting bracken-starch mochi wrapped around plenty of smooth bean paste and buried in fragrant kinako, three for ¥940. It is made for the day and goes to reservations first, ready from about 12:30, so phone ahead or reserve the day before; walk-ins often find only a sample in the case. Staff are warm. Eat it the same day. Cash only; closed Wednesday and Thursday.

kyoto_imanishi_ken.gf_detail: Ask. Ohagi are glutinous rice with bean paste or kinako; no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
kyoto_imanishi_ken.vegan_detail: Ask. Rice, azuki and kinako ohagi are likely candidates, but no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
kyoto_imanishi_ken.hours_raw: From 9:30 until sold out — 8:00 during the equinox weeks; closed Tuesday and the first, third and fifth Monday, and both Monday and Tuesday in July and August (Tabelog). With no fixed closing time, no hours are stored. A queue of 15–20 forms before opening; kinako sells out first (September–October 2026). Reservations accepted by 14:00 (Tabelog). Takeaway. Cash only (Tabelog). 1–2 min from Gojo Stn exit 4 (Tabelog). The shop closed in 1995 and reopened in 2002 (Tabelog).
kyoto_imanishi_ken.notes: [Wagashi · Gojo, the ohagi queue] A tiny shop a minute from Gojo Station that makes just three kinds of ohagi — kinako, smooth bean paste and chunky bean paste — at ¥240 each, until they are gone. The rice is soft and only partly mashed, the paste gently sweet; the kinako goes first, often before 10:00. Expect 15–20 people waiting at the 9:30 opening (8:00 around the equinox), or reserve before 14:00. Cash only; closed Tuesdays and some Mondays, and both days in July and August.
